name.text: True or false course track and drift

questiontext.text:
For each statement, choose true or false.

(a) [[if test="is(it1=1)"]]When there is no current, the track is the same as the course.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=2)"]]The ground speed is always more than the speed through the water.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=3)"]]The drift angle is the angle between the course and the track.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=4)"]]The track is the direction in which the boat is pointed.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=5)"]]A wind blowing from \(270^\circ\) pushes an aircraft towards the east.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=6)"]]A current flowing towards \(090^\circ\) and a wind blowing from \(090^\circ\) push in the same direction.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=7)"]]If the current flows in the same direction as the course, the drift angle is \(0^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=8)"]]To travel straight across a river, a boat must be steered partly upstream.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=9)"]]The ground speed is found by adding the boat's speed and the current's speed.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=10)"]]When the current is at right angles to the course, the ground speed is \(\sqrt{\text{boat speed}^2 + \text{current speed}^2}\).[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=11)"]]Doubling the speed of a current at right angles to the course doubles the drift angle.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=12)"]]A boat steered at right angles to a current takes the same time to cross a river as it would in still water.[[/if]] [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The course is where the boat points, the track is where it goes, and the drift angle is the angle between them. Velocities add as arrows: course velocity \(+\) current velocity \(=\) track velocity.

  • (a) [[if test="is(kk[1]=1)"]]True[[else]]False[[/if]]. [[if test="is(it1=1)"]]With no current the velocity triangle collapses: the boat goes where it points.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=2)"]]A current against the boat, or across it at a wide angle, can make the ground speed smaller.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=3)"]]That is the definition used in this chapter.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=4)"]]The boat points along its course. The track is where it actually goes.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=5)"]]Winds are named by where they come from: from \(270^\circ\) (west) means towards \(090^\circ\) (east).[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=6)"]]The current pushes east; a wind from \(090^\circ\) pushes west.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=7)"]]Then all three arrows lie along one line.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=8)"]]Steering upstream cancels the current's sideways push.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=9)"]]Velocities add as arrows, by the triangle; speeds add only when the arrows point the same way.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=10)"]]The triangle is right-angled with the ground speed as hypotenuse.[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=11)"]]\(\tan d\) doubles, not \(d\) itself: for example \(\tan^{-1}(0.2) = 11.3^\circ\) but \(\tan^{-1}(0.4) = 21.8^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(it1=12)"]]The current only moves it sideways; the speed across is unchanged.[[/if]]

questiondescription.text:
Navigation: course, track and drift

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.7 (f): Decide whether statements about course, track, drift, currents and winds are true or false.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).
